messages:
Ava: Quick RFC follow-up: we need an explicit ownership contract for preemptible windows — when a lane yields mid-window how do we guarantee KV cache reuse and safe handoff?
kevin: Agree. Current implicit handoff is causing KV cache thrash on spikes. We should define a 3-way handshake: owner, releaser, taker.
maria: Do we have telemetry to detect handoff-induced cache misses? I saw a 12% spike during last canary.
infra-bot: deploy status: canary #2026 passed metrics gating (latency ok)
kevin: Proposal snippet:
```
1) owner marks slot 'releasing' with lease_token
2) taker polls release queue with token and prefetches key ranges
3) owner confirms 'released' and decrements headroom
```
Jin: How do we prevent long-tail waits when taker is slow? backpressure? fallback to global pool?
Ava: Two fallbacks: (a) if no taker within T_handshake -> owner drains and marks keys cold; (b) route new requests to cold-path (global pool) with higher cost tag.
maria: Need SLA metrics: handshake latency, cache-miss rate post-handoff, preempted-requests ratio.
ops-qa: can we expose a sampling trace ID for each handshake? that'll help root-cause.
Leo: Also consider partial handoffs: move hot prefixes only. less KV copy, but adds complexity to slot accounting.
kevin: Agree. Let's aim for minimal viable contract for v1: token handshake + timeout fallback + telemetry events. We can iterate on partial handoff later.
Ava: I'll draft a short RFC addendum with the proto + sample telemetry fields. @maria @Jin can you review tomorrow? :thumbsup:
maria: Ack. I can review after standup.
Jin: I'll run a sim for worst-case taker latency and post numbers.
infra-bot: incident-alert: none
Ava: thanks — keeping this small will let us ship the escape hatch quickly.
